title: Alternative employment can preserve work while transferring lower pay and travel costs after site-clearance loss
source_unit: Fair Work Commission Bulletin Volume 4/25, item 3, summarizing a mining employment unfair-dismissal and compensation decision

observations.period: September 2024–April 3, 2025; site-clearance revocation, dismissal, alternative job, and compensation order

denominator.unit: publicly summarized adjudicated worker case; no population denominator

alternative_employment_start.unit: weeks after dismissal; exact dismissal date not reported

compensation_receipt.unit: missing payment date, channel, receipt, tax, and residual-loss evidence

original_job_restoration.value: not observed; alternative employment rather than reinstatement

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Commission bulletin summary; site-clearance control, employer termination/redeployment, alternative employment, lower pay and travel burden, and ordered compensation are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: One case cannot estimate dismissal, alternative-employment, travel-burden, remedy, or payment rates. The bulletin does not report claimant identity, exact dates, wage amounts, hours, job duration, household effects, trust, recurrence, or later exit.
observations.subgroup: One drive-in/drive-out mining worker whose client site clearance was revoked and whose contractor found no suitable nearby redeployment.
observations.counterinterpretation: A replacement job can prevent immediate unemployment while reducing pay and increasing travel costs; an ordered compensation amount does not prove payment, adequacy, or restoration of the original opportunity.

related_sources.claim: Official Fair Work Commission decision and bulletin search route.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the committed project ledger containing the bounded bulletin extraction.
reproduction_audit.access_boundary: The public bulletin reports alternative employment and an ordered remedy but not payment receipt, job duration, household recovery, trust, recurrence, collective action, or exit.

boundary: This record adds one public case in which alternative employment is observed alongside lower pay, travel burden, and a compensation order after site-clearance loss. It does not establish payment receipt, full recovery, prevalence, durable work, trust, action, recurrence, switching, or exit.
